title: A must-have
text:
It's big, very big, and wanting to see everything is a challenge. First, get a skip-the-line ticket, you will quickly have the satisfaction of having spent a little money. The museum's collections are very varied (Roman and Egyptian antiquities, sculptures, paintings, frescoes, etc.)
The apartments of the former Popes decorated by Raphael are true marvels. All possible circuits end at the Sistine Chapel, of which, it is well known, the ceiling is by Michelangelo. About the ceiling, I expected the creation of Adam to be the major theme, but that's only a small part of the ceiling. Well it's magnificent.
Be careful, there are also a lot of groups who don't care about the other visitors. Also note that the plan provided is not very intuitive and that the signage could be improved.
Also note during our visit the presence of works by Dali, Van Gogh, Rodin, etc.

placeInfo.name: Vatican Museums
placeInfo.address: Viale Vaticano, 00120 Vatican City Italy

title: Direct Prime Experience tour with early access and breakfast.
text:
I am so glad I was able to purchase this tour directly from the Vatican site.  I cannot find the tour here, so here is my review.

The tour started at 7:30 but we were led in at 7:15.  There were only 4 groups of about 20 people, that started in sequence.  We had the whole museums to ourselves.  It was so impressive.  our guide was very knowledgeable and I learned a lot, either on Vatican history OR on the rooms that we saw.  Of course, the Rafael room were very impressive.  We felt alone and so peaceful.  We were able to take excellent pictures.

Then we went to the Sixtine Chapel.  Our guide, as it was early entry, could whisper to us and point things.  This is not the case in later visits.  We could also sit down on the benches to look up.  It was very amazing.

Then we were led to breakfast, which was included in our price.  At that point, its about 10:30, so I was glad that we had breakfast beforehand.  Breakfast was a good american breakfast with eggs and bacon.

Then, we decided to go back through the Sixtine Chapel to use the secret path to St-Peters Basilica.  However, we couldn't backtrack and had to start over the whole sequence.  oh boy, it took us about 20 minutes re-walking through very intense crowds to get there.  Everything was roped off and you had to follow packed like sardines.  I never would have suffered through 2 hours of this.  Ensure you tickets are pre-opening!

Back at the Sixtine Chapel, we could use the path as we had had a tour, and go straight to St-Peters without having to go back outside re-line for security.

Very worth it.

placeInfo.name: Vatican Museums
placeInfo.address: Viale Vaticano, 00120 Vatican City Italy

title: INESTIMABLE VALUE, SORRY ABOUT THE EXCESSIVE CROWD
text:
The Vatican museums must be seen at least once in a lifetime, the works are of indescribable beauty, the value is inestimable.
I went to these museums on a weekday in September and there was an incredible crowd.
It is impossible to pass through in some places (e.g. in the Round Room, Candelabra Gallery, etc.), as groups with guides linger for a long time, invading the entire space, rather than standing to the side and leaving free passage for independent visitors , so I had to push past to make my way.
They should divide the entrances with and without guides, otherwise you risk losing works as you are intent on creating the passage and looking for a glimpse of air, often you couldn't breathe!!!.
The experience in the Sistine Chapel was beautiful, but excessively crowded, DO NOT take photos, there are many security personnel who will remind you, and may ask you to delete it, rather carry a memory in your heart.
Book your tickets, avoid endless queues, I had taken the one with lunch included, as there was no other availability. Food is served in the self-service restaurant on floor -1, where you can get a first and second course, water and fruit/yoghurt or dessert delivered by the staff. Fair/good quality.
Excellent toilet facilities.
The route is well highlighted, follow it carefully, and don't rush through the Sistine Chapel, the other rooms are also worth it, especially the Art Gallery, often overlooked, but with spatial masterpieces (Perugino, Caravaggio, Raphael, Leonardo) and also the art department Borgia Apartment/Modern Art with Dalì, Chagall, Morandi and the beautiful Pietà by Van Gogh there was almost no one here!!
Definitely a positive cultural experience.

title: WORST ATTRACTION IN ITALY
text:
Few bathrooms, filthy, small, dirty.
Rude and rude attendants, a crowd of people in tight spaces, walking extremely slowly.
Many rude people stop along the way to take photos and selfies (without even observing or admiring), completely disturbing the passage (making it even more tiring)...
Rude guides who stop halfway to explain as if the Vatican were theirs. In fact, the guides ruin the tour.
Poor infrastructure. Very few bathrooms, but souvenir shops have a lot.
Even in St. Peter's Basilica there is only one bathroom outside (side basement), but inside the Basilica there are countless little shops. In other words, money is what matters. This says a lot about how the church thinks.
The few bathrooms are crowded, tiny, hot and filthy.
You pay dearly for a horrible ride.
The worst thing about the Vatican is the path to the Sistine Chapel. They create a corral system forcing people to pass through wings without any expressiveness, making the journey to the Sistine chapel extremely tiring. Truly, a penance.
If you put together everything that is really interesting in the Vatican museums, it doesn't fill a room.
Terrible restaurants and cafes with rude staff. It seems that the tourist is the biggest inconvenience. But everything is expensive.

The worst tour in Italy, tourist trap.

title: Essential, but really busy
text:
Museum contained many interesting surprises, however was hard to navigate and few maps available. It was easy to get lost, especially close to the entrance.

Plenty of facilities on site including gift shops and a cafe, but exceptionally busy. Recommended booking in advance as queue to enter can take hours. There were also few places to sit and rest inside the museum - a lot of walking is required.

The Sistine Chapel makes the visit worth while, but hard to view the exhibits close to this as they really herd the crowds through them with guards advising not to stop. This is a shame, as it meant we couldn't view the gorgeous tapestries and maps at leasure.

Worth a visit but be warned - very busy! Additionally, visitors note that you have to leave the museum and walk around the outside of the city wall to reach Saint Peter's - not an issue, but it wasn't initially that clear!

placeInfo.name: Vatican Museums
placeInfo.address: Viale Vaticano, 00120 Vatican City Italy

title: Glorious and thrumming with activity
text:
So let me preface by saying that the Vatican Museums house some of the most breathtakingly glorious Catholic artwork in existence - there are thousands upon thousands of pieces of art in here.  You could wander through these museums for days and still not have time to look at everything.  It's very, very clear that they revere this artwork as a testament to the power of the Vatican.

With that being said, I strongly recommend that people buy their tickets ahead of time to expedite the entry process, as it is utterly jam-packed.  There are people in every nook and cranny of the museums, which is overwhelming and a bit irritating when you want to take a moment to look at the artwork - there's always someone jostling you, so you never have enough time to look at everything you want to see.  Tours are good if you're interested, but because it's so busy, you can generally overhear everything anyway.  I wish they would offer timed tickets to minimize the crowds.

placeInfo.name: Vatican Museums

title: People packed in like sardines.
text:
Let’s start with the positive.   The Vatican museum has an incredible collection of art and antiques.

Sadly the negative massively outweighed it.   People were packed in like Sardines.   There was no way you could stop and linger, admiring a painting.  You were just forced to shuffle forward.    

Any other major museum has timed tickets, which control the numbers.   Sadly The Vatican has learned it can charge what it likes and pack people in like sardines.

I didn’t honestly feel much of this collection was displayed properly.   It really did remind me of a Greedy Art Collector, happy to own precious art works, but not prepared to display and research them properly.

title: Amazing place; poor tour
text: We booked the prime experience direct with the Vatican; this included breakfast and a tour that started at 7.30am. Downsides: even though we were in a small group of ‘just’ 26, we were surrounded by numerous other small groups. While it still was less crammed than it would have been later in the day, it was definitely still very busy.  Second, we were disappointed by our tour guide. She pushed us out of the way while we were queuing to pick our pre-booked tickets up, and for the first 20 mins or so spent longer talking about her own physical ailments than the stunning surroundings we were in. It really detracted; at one point I pulled the earpiece out altogether. She clearly knew a lot of detail but there was no sense of clear tour narrative. A particular highlight was when she moaned about another guide who innocently asked her how she’d hurt her leg. I’m pretty forgiving in general but this was a bad tour.

title: Beautiful must see if visiting Rome!
text:
We visited St Peter’s during our five day stay in Rome. We did make the mistake of visiting at midday and therefore stood in the queue for 1.5 hours in the blazing 34 degree heat which was uncomfortable at times! However, this is a free site, and if timed rightly, can be done much more easily. When we left, the queue had already drastically reduced and the temperature had cooled a little. I’d say about 3pm is a great time to visit. 

Inside is just breathtaking, and it truly is worth a visit just to admire the beauty of this attraction. 

Tip: for any religious sites in Rome, you are required to cover your shoulders/ thighs. I hadn’t been aware of this so when I arrived, they offered out free covers to cover knees/ shoulders for those who were exposed, so don’t be tempted to spend a lot of money panic buying scarfs from the street vendors!

title: A “must see” site
text:
One of the “must-see” sites to any visit of Rome. This is one of the most holiest sites of the Catholic faith and the Basilica is a masterpiece of architecture, art, history and symbolism. Pls note that there is a dress code for all visitors — no shorts or skirts above the knees and no bare shoulders or hats permitted. 
In any case, the Basilica was sublime — just to the right as you enter is Michelangelos’ Pieta , straight ahead  is his majestic dome along with Bernini’s bronze altar canopy — other artworks abound. One can also climb the dome or visit the burial grottos inside.

title: A place where religions and history turns alive!
text:
Vatican City is the world's smallest city state and lie within the precincts of Rome and visitors to Rome will usually make a stop to visit this country that though small but control 1/5 of the world populations, Roman Catholics (RC)!

Going into the Vatican is easy and one does not need passport or visa and by just crossing a barricade, you are already in another country. The buildings around are spectacular and nice, and of course stood the test of time and religious "politics" for centuries.

And do note of the great number of people, local and visitors rushing to come here to visit and for many, to feel the presence of God and strengthen their faith and hope. Of course, one needs the patient to queue to get into the cathedral to visit (with security check) but it's worth it. Although I am not a RC, I am impressed of the massive paintings, statues, decors all around and how each tell their own story.

This visit reminded me of my previous visit to Fatima in Portugal, as some of the buildings, chapels and buildings seemed aka alike. It's also another sacred place RC will make pilgrimage to, besides this one!

And on certain days like Wednesday or Sunday, masses are held and many will just flock here to have an audience with their Papa Pope.

You can also visit the Sistine Chapel, the Museum and even the Post Office to get local souvenirs.

So whether you are a RC or not, it's worth coming for a visit, at least eye-opening experience and learn new things.

title: Spellbinding
text:
There’s no excuse not to visit St. Peter’s Basilica if you’re already in Rome. The Vatican deserves a full day at least, and St. Peter’s is one of the primary reasons for that. The building is adorned with the most spectacular decoration, palates, and textures…no picture does justice.

It is free to enter, but there are security checks, and with lines during peak seasons, waiting to enter can take long. As a wheelchair user, I was somewhat expedited in…part of my inevitable disability privilege. Once inside, accessibility is omnipresent. The spaces were filled with tourists, but due to St. Peter’s grand size, it never felt claustrophobic.

Dress appropriately, respect religious functions, and speak softly…this ensures your visit will be fantastic for you and fellow guests. Enjoy! St. Peter’s Basilica is an absolute must-do.

text:

We had an early start to our day as we had to reach the meeting point by 7:15 am. We entered the Vatican Museums by 8 am along with the rest of our group. Claudia, our guide, was excellent. title: A fascinating place - not hugely accessible though!
text:
I visited the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel with my husband and 1 year old son in May 2023. There was a lot to see and you can get a guided tour. With a 1 year old, we chose not to get a guided tour so that we could move around in our own time and not be constantly with people moving us along. We felt that this gave us the ability to freely see what we wanted to see and not be rushed or slowed down by groups.

We took a pushchair for my son and on the whole it was easy to wheel this around each floor. WARNING: there is a lift up to the first/second level but after this, once you're moving through the museum to the Sistine Chapel, there are a lot of stairs! There wasn't anywhere that indicated that there was a lift, so I don't think one existed past allowing you to go up to the first level. I ended up carrying the buggy up and down the stairs with my husband (and I was pregnant at the time - not ideal!! - but there wasn't any other way to do it, so I just got on with it).

The Sistine Chapel was amazing (although it takes a long time to get through the rest of the Museum to see it). It's very peaceful. The security guards were great, on the whole, at stopping people from taking photos within the Sistine Chapel, although I saw some tourists still sneaking a few photos when they weren't being watched, which was disappointing.

On the whole, this was a great visit and the artwork was fantastic. It's a visit I'll never forget!

title: Nice place but....
text:
If we talk about the museum and the works of art present, we can only give it the highest score, beautiful and very interesting, and it is something that you cannot fail to visit.
But the weak point is the organisation, we visited it by booking well in advance and with a tour guide, but the real problem we experienced was the crowds inside which did not allow us to fully enjoy the experience, even the guide, who was very good, was in great difficulty, and he had to play down the situation, he struggled to find a "gap" for us to stop and tell us about the beauties present, we had to pass through many rooms without stopping and he told us while walking, without considering the absurd heat that was there (which is strange as in a museum there should usually be a constant and cool temperature to avoid the deterioration of the works), I think we were far out of the norm in terms of the number of people inside.
The tour also included a visit to the Sistine Chapel, keeping in mind that the Guide informed us that as it was a place of worship you couldn't talk and you couldn't take photos, so he explained and told us everything in front of the monitors where they were all the works were projected inside, it's a shame that when we entered the Sistine Chapel there was real "chaos" and everyone was taking photos, the poor guards present were trying to silence and forbid photos but no one was listening to them, and we had to elbow our way to see something.
I gave 4 stars because it's a nice place because it deserves them all, but overall a bad experience, a bad organization, it's a shame because they have a treasure in their hands, they have a long way to go.

title: LA VERGOGNA.
text:
Dell’ opera d’arte in se non possiamo certo parlare.
Una meraviglia assoluta che sfida il tempo.
Un patrimonio inestimabile dell’ umanità.

Ma proprio per questo non dovrebbe essere mercificata e ridotta in questo stato.

All’ ingresso ci sono le seguenti indicazioni:

- STARE IN SILENZIO
- NON FOTOGRAFARE
- DIVIETO DELL’ USO DEL CELLULARE

Bene, dopo una coda disumana eccoci all’ ingresso della Cappella…

Stare in Silenzio?
Orde di visitatori di tutte le nazionalità sono intenti a parlare del più e del meno, a commentare, a chiamarsi anche ad alta voce. Bambini sbraitano, mamme rimproverano, fidanzati amoreggiano. E fra tutto questo, a voce ancora più alta, le guardie/automi che, meccanicamente, ripetono “No Foto, No Foto”… ad libitum.

Divieto dell’ uso del cellulare?
Ma anche no! Ho visto gente in videochat mostrarsi nella cappella e commentare in diretta l’ esperienza o tizi parlare con mamma tutti orgogliosi del posto dove stavano.

Ma la cosa più bella è il “Non Fotografare”.
Credetemi, amici e lettori, gli unici (e sottolineo “gli unici”) a non scattare foto e fare riprese video in tutto lo spazio della Cappella Sistina siamo stati io e la mia Famigliola.
Gli unici.
Fra foto volanti, foto posate, selfie, riprese anche a 360 gradi e GoPro impazzite è stato tutto un orgasmo multimediale incredibile.
E sempre nel mezzo i soliti personaggi (inutili, a questo punto), che strombazzavano il loro “No Foto, No Foto”.

Praticamente un orgione disumano assurdo (ogni minimo centimetro dell’area calpestabile era utilizzato) che sembravamo a Milano in Piazza Duomo la notte del fine millennio scorso.
Con la differenza che questa non è una piazza, ma un luogo sacro, e non siamo a fine millennio, ma in un banale giorno dell’anno qualsiasi.

Capisco, capisco benissimo la voglia di lor signori vaticani di far cassetta con le loro opere d’arte, ma questa cosa ha del patetico e del vergognoso.
Calmierare gli ingressi facendo entrare dalle 25 alle 50 persone per volta permetterebbe almeno di poter ottenere il rispetto delle regole ed una fruizione quantomeno ottimale dell’ opera tutta.
Invece tu entri fra centinaia e centinaia di “animali” allo stato brado, sbattuto di qua e di la dalle spinte della gente, impossibilitato anche solo a rimaner fermo ad osservare un particolare, con l’ unico pensiero che è quello di uscire velocemente dal sito prima possibile.
Che indegnità.
Qua si che ci sarebbe voluto un Cristo a buttar fuori i mercanti (e gli acquirenti) dal tempio a frustrate…

Osceno.

title: Awesome frescoes
text: The Sistine Chapel is inside the Apostolic Palace in Vatican City and accessible via the Vatican Museums. The Chapel is named after Sixtus IV , the pope who commissioned it in the 1470s. THe Chapel is a brick building shaped like a rectangle. The outside is plain, with no decoration and no big door. It has six arched windows on its two side walls . The pavement of the chapel is a combination of marble and a colored stone that marks the processional way from the main door that the Pope follows on Palm Sunday. The ceiling is not flat like a canvas but a complex set of curves created by the structural elements of the roof. Pope Julius II commissioned Michelangelo to paint the ceiling. Look out too for the frescoes where Adam and God touch fingers, the Last Judgement and The Last Supper.  The Chapel is more than an artistic masterpiece as it is. A place of crucial religious activity. Since 1492, the Chapel has been the site where theCollege of Cardinals gathers to elect a new pope.

title: Semplicemente Ricca
text: Inutile dire che in tutta San Pietro quello che domina è l’oro, la ricchezza e lo sfarzo della Chiesa e la Cupola di San Pietro non è da meno. Acquistati i biglietti con 8€ si fa l’intera salita a piedi degli oltre 600 scalini. L’ascensore non ne vale la pena perché arriva solo alla prima tappa, si evitano gli scalini più facili e c’è sempre coda. Finiti i primi 250 scalini fortunatamente c’è un ristoro e si può ammirare la cupola dall’interno da un ballatoio che gli gira tutto intorno. I mosaici sono pazzeschi, fatti di vetro di Murano con colori e precisione incredibile. Poi arriva la parte più difficile: oltre 300 scalini molto stretti, a volte in pendenza e che salgono a chiocciola e può girare la testa. Con un passo lento e costante ce la si può fare. Arrivati in cima il panorama è impagabile: si vede tutto il piazzale di San Pietro, i giardini della Basilica e gran parte di Roma, peccato solo fosse nuvolo. Sconsigliato a chi è sovrappeso semplicemente perché non passa dai scalini stretti.

title: Basilique Saint Pierre
text:
La basilique Saint-Pierre est l’un des plus grands monuments du monde et un des plus visités, longue de 218 mètres et dont le dôme culmine à 133 mètres au dessus du sol. Accueillant le Saint-Siège, cet édifice religieux est le plus important et le plus vaste de l’église catholique, au cœur de cette dernière, où le Pape célèbre les principales liturgies.
En effet, sur le site du cirque de Caligula et de Néron, l’empereur Constantin Ier éleva ici la première basilique, devenue la destination des premiers pèlerins se rendant à Rome pour rendre le culte à saint Pierre. Car la tradition catholique place la tombe de saint Pierre sous le maître-autel et le grand baldaquin, au centre de l’église.
Cette grandiose basilique est inscrite au patrimoine de l’Unesco, à plus d’un titre, ayant été dès son édification considérée comme la plus vaste œuvre architecturale. Elle fut réalisée entre 1506 et 1626, avec la majestueuse place Saint-Pierre qui lui fait face, à laquelle œuvrèrent les plus grands artistes et architectes de l’époque, comme Michel-Ange, Bramante, Maderno ou le Bernin.

title: wahres Wunderwerk der Architektur

Der Innenraum ist wunderschön und prächtig, mit seinen reich verzierten Wänden und Decken, die mit kunstvollen Fresken und Mosaiken verziert sind. Der Altarraum ist ein wahres Meisterwerk, das durch seine aufwändige Verzierung und seine prächtige Ausstattung beeindruckt. Es ist ein Ort voller Ehrfurcht und Bewunderung und man kann sich nur schwer vorstellen, wie viel Arbeit in die Errichtung dieses Meisterwerks gesteckt wurde. Die Kirche ist ein wahrhaftiges Wunder der Architektur und eine einzigartige Erfahrung. Es ist ein Ort, an dem man sich in Ehrfurcht und Bewunderung versenken kann, während man die prächtigen und aufwändigen Details bewundert.

title: Be your own guide & save money!
text:
Firstly entry into the cathedral itself is free although many of the tour guides leave you with the impression that it’s not. We booked a tour through Expedia sold as ‘skip the line, direct access, small group’ - but owning to poor redemption instructions we missed it. We even called the tour company at the right time we were supposed to meet and they did nothing to help or clarify the wrong instructions and just said 20 other people made it so ‘sorry - just try and find your guide’. Would not even make contact for us to establish exact location. A Wasted €100. Another misleading claim about it being a ‘small group’ - 20 people is not a small group! 

Still we were there and so decided to do our own self tour if we could. We went through security and within 2 minutes was in the beautiful awe inspiring cathedral. We definitely recommend going early morning, say around 8am. When we came out later in the morning the queue for security was around the whole length of the square.

Once inside we also discovered access to the Cupla and Dome with amazing views overlooking the Vatican was only €8. You can pay up to €70pp (we paid €50pp) for a tour and yet it’s only €8 to do it all yourself. We much prefer this. The tour groups were massive, very slow paced and seemed disengaged. 

Note, you really need good mobility to go to the outside part of the Dome. It involves some 500 steps some of which are very steep in narrow spaces. You can pay €14 to get an elevator but that only gets you as far as the first roof and not the Cupla itself which will still include clambering around 200 steps.

Please also visit at night where there is hardly any people and where the cathedral looks stunning. You obviously can’t go inside at night.

title: Beautiful Church and Pleasant on a Weekday
text:
We went to the Basilica after our Vatican Museums tour and got into the Basilica quickly around 11:30 am. There are lots of things to see but if you want to see the grottoes or the dome it is recommended to line up early. The dome costs a few Euros so we opted for the Grottoes which were free. We queued up and spent about 15 minutes in the grottoes and most signs were in English and were interesting to read. The Basilica is large so if you want to see everything expect to spend an hour or more inside. At the exit there is a free drinking water fountain so you can fill your bottle here.

It is open from 7 am to 7 pm according to the Vatican's website and you may want to consider getting there early if it is something you want to see. Entrance is free to the square and Basilica and there is no need to get a ticket on normal days. There are dress codes so dress modestly if you are going here. An hour should be enough time but you could spend more if you attend a service. Tour guides seem to be permitted and I'd you're interested enough you could get one or find a self guided tour or audio guide on your phone. On Wednesdays there is a Papal service but you need to get a free ticket to enter.

Ottaviano is the closest metro but the busses are very good getting around Rome as well. Getting here early is best and you may want to consider food shoes while walking through the Vatican Museums. If you plan to see the museums and St. Peter's area it is suggested you buy your tickets in advance for the Vatican Museums and set at least 4 hours aside to see both the Museums, Basilica and Square.

The Sistine Chapel is a place that I had always heard about and when I finally walked into it, it was initially underwhelming.
However when I started to take some time to absorb the stories being told through Michelangelo’s art, it became mesmerising. It is like one giant story painted into a ceiling, with all the pieces connecting in perfect ways.
The chapel doesn’t feel holy or spiritual in any way because there are so many tourists but that doesn’t take away from the beauty of the work

title: Indimenticabile
text:
Parto col dire che la cupola è una delle cose per le quali i turisti vengono a Roma e sicuramente è un'esperienza che ti resta dentro, quello che critico invece è la pessima organizzazione proprio per la salita sulla cupola, senza criterio e senza indicazioni. Abbiamo pagato 10 euro a testa sapendo che l'ascensore ci avrebbe portati fino alla cima invece poi abbiamo scoperto che l'ascensore ci aveva "risparmiato" un centinaio di scalini o poco più mentre il resto dovevamo farcelo tutto a piedi, non considerando e soprattutto non sapendo che la cupola presenta degli scalini molto stretti, perlopiù a chiocciola, e che la salita di essi non è adatta a tutti. 
Parlo per mia esperienza, soffrendo di pressione bassa ma avendo fatto altri tipi di escursioni, mi sono sentita male e purtroppo sono dovuta riscendere obbligatoriamente non usufruendo appieno del biglietto, sono scesa in totale autonomia una volta ripresa perché lì la linea tra l'altro poco prende e dubito che i paramedici avrebbero potuto soccorrere me e chi è sceso con me. Sicuramente non è una attrazione adatta a tutti, ma scriverlo prima magari su un grande cartello avrebbe risparmiato a me la paura di rimanerci.
La cosa bella è la cupola dall'interno, vedere quell'arte preziosa a pochi metri di distanza ha creato stupore e meraviglia in me, proprio una piacevole pausa prima dell'abisso.

title: Ritornare...
text:
Sono ritornata qui dopo qualche anno e ho trovato alcuni cambiamenti che sicuramente sono dettati da motivi di sicurezza, per carità, però onestamente alcuni sono totalmente fuori luogo. Fine immense ed interminabili, non una segnaletica e nemmeno qualcuno che sappia indicare Dove bisogna recarsi o cosa vedere. La basilica comunque è grandissima, molto alta rispetto alle altre che ho visto ed ha un valore architettonico, culturale, religioso molto importante. 
Sicuramente da visitare in un giorno più tranquillo perché le persone, quelle maleducate che pensano solo a fotografare e non si curano dei fedeli, non sanno stare in un luogo sacro e intaccano il momento di preghiera che soprattutto lì è d'obbligo.

title: Better to go later when most of the crowds have vamoosed
text: Go later., I went around 5:30. No ticket and maybe a 10 min wait at security. The basilica is awesome in its sheer size and the space is vast. It’s not my favourite church, not even close but it is the seat of Roman Catholicism and there is an imperiousness about it that exudes pomp power and majesty. Not very Christian attributes you might say and you might be right but when all is said and done this is one of the most important buildings in the world and is redolent with implications and is symbol of faith for hundreds of millions of Catholics of which I am one. I was absolutely thrilled when 6pm arrived and there was a mass in the chapel designed by Bernini in the apse behind the Baldacchino. I really wanted to attend is at was something my parents and parents in law wanted to do but never did and now I could do it in remembrance of them . Very special and talking about special don’t think of leaving without viewing the Pieta by Michelangelo. Just a stunning piece of sculpture. Afterwards take a stroll around St Peter’s Square and the colonnades as the sun goes down. Magic and great for the soul.

title: Majestic
text:
I have been to many Cathedrals but I was not prepared for the grandeur of this place!

We came to Rome during Easter and the aim of course was to see if we could attend mass. Until about a week before our visit, we were convinced that we didn’t need tickets, we could just walk in. It was only by chance when I was doing my final research that I noted it was essential to get tickets if you wanted to be anywhere near the pope. The tickets are free, you email a form to the Vatican using an email provided on their website and then if you are lucky, you will get an email back with a number and you collect the tickets inside St Peter’s square. Information held online suggested that the tickets are in demand, especially for major holidays like Easter and also for the masses led by The Pope. They indicate that those who are keen, should apply for tickets 6-2 months in advance. Well, I applied for mine 4 days before and did not expect anything back, imagine my shock when I got an email back with ticket numbers. It is easy finding out which masses the pope will be leading, there is a schedule posted online.

The mass was due to start at around 9.30. We had read reviews that suggested the queues can be horrendous so the aim was to arrive early. We were there by 8am. There was no queue, we went through security within 5 minutes. When we collected our tickets, our sitting place was right at the front! 

The square is amazing, exactly the way it looks on TV. It’s hard to imagine the sheer numbers of people who attend. When we attended on Easter Sunday, there was an indication that there were over 30 000 people in attendance!

Attending mass here is an experience. I couldn’t tell you what the service was about because the mass was in Italian!  

We had the opportunity to walk around the square after mass. It is beautiful. 

The following day, we booked a tour with the Tour Guy. We had the opportunity to see inside the Cathedral. Words cannot describe how beautiful this place is. I am usually behind the camera taking pictures of everything I see, I didn’t know where to look here! We also had the opportunity to attend mass inside the Cathedral, of course, this is not led by the pope but regular services conducted throughout the day led by different priests, this is in Italian too.

The volume of people going into the Sistine Chapel is crazy, get there early to make the most of it. It seemed to get more crowded towards lunch time.

The Sistine Chapel is beautiful, the architecture and artwork are breathtaking. As you make your way from the Vatican Museum into the Chapel you go through a long long corridor which is also beautifully painted. 

We visited as part of a self guided tour that covered both the Sistine Chapel and the Vatican Museum. Both were amazing to see.

We also managed to have a walk around St Peter's Basilica within the same day.

title: Für mich enttäuschend
text:
Die Sixtinische Kapelle mit all ihren Fresken selbst ist wahnsinnig beeindruckend und ein absolutes Must-see. Meine Bewertung bezieht sich daher nicht auf das Bau- und Kunstwerk an sich sondern auf meinen Besuch dort. 
Der war für mich eher enttäuschend. Es hatte absolut nichts von einer Kapelle oder auch nur kirchlicher Atmosphäre. Statt Kirchenbänken in denen man sitzen und die einmalige Decke bewundern kann, war der Raum vollgestopft mit Menschen. Der im Raum umlaufende Steinsims war von Menschen belegt, der überwiegende Teil der Menschen stand in der Mitte. 
Obwohl mehrfach durch das Ordnerpersonal zur Ruhe gemahnt wurde, ist der wenig besinnliche Geräuschpegel durch hunderte von Menschen unvermeidbar. Die Luft ist stickig und es ist heiß. 
Ich fand es kaum möglich in Ruhe die Fresken an der Decke und den Wänden zu betrachten, weil man ständig angerempelt wurde. 
Nach der ebenso wenig erfreulichen Tour durch die Vatikanischen Museen hatte ich den Eindruck, dass ich mein Geld lieber anderweitig investiert hätte. Sehr schade.

title: Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel Visit on 16th January IGNORE TOUTS
text:
Ignore the touts selling tickets for group tours. Instead, purchase ticket from the official ticket office inside the museum entrance, at the top of the stairs. We spent longer trying to avoid the ticket touts, and disengage ourselves from conversation with them, than we did queuing. Our visit was late morning (11:30 ish), we queued for perhaps 5 minutes at the most to purchase our ticket and get through security. 

Outside the front entrance there our signs that say something along the lines of ‘Tour Operator Partners..’. It looks like the entrance is just for tour operators but it is in fact the main entrance - despite people telling you as you walk up that you need to have pre-booked tickets. Once again, ignore the touts and go inside the vatican museum entrance - go upstairs to purchase a ticket. There is the option to purchase guided  tour tickets inside if that’s something you want to do - we didn’t. 

We also went to St Peter’s Basilica and up the dome. At at around 3pm, it took about 20 minutes to queue and get through security. There was no queue to purchase tickets for the dome. Cash only to buy the dome tickets. 

Week after epiphany seems like a good time to visit!

title: De fazer parar a respiração.....
text:
A Capela Sistina é um dos maiores tesouros do Vaticano e, na minha opinião, um dos maiores do Mundo. Conhecida pelos seus frescos e local onde os Papas são escolhidos e coroados ( a coroação só acaba quando são investidos como Bispo de Roma ).
Totalmente coberta por frescos, Botticelli, Perugino,Luca e Michelangelo, é o teto que nos parar a respiração. Obra de Mechelangelo, as nove histórias do Génesis a famosa e lindíssima criação de Adão e, sobre o altar maior, o Juízo Final que representa o Apocalipse. Estas obras parecem que têm “ vida “. 
Dado não ser permitido fotos da capela, deixo 3 fotos de placares, situados nos jardins do Vaticano e onde nos foi explicado o significado dos frescos pela guia à qual desde já quero agradecer a sua simpatia e profissionalismo.
Aconselho a visita guiada. O preço não é nada comparado com o que se aprende.
Visita obrigatória !!!

However, if you expect to just turn up and go in it seems that is no longer possible. This is my fourth trip to Rome so I remember the old days. Now it too seems over run with tourists who simply what to look which means lines zig zag bag through the square mixing those who what to climb the dome with those who simply wish to go and pray. You can stand in these lines for hours as people and tour groups jostle and push for position because they think they are more important than you? Or are they just selfish? I wonder if it was a line for confession if you would see so much keenness and pushing?

title: Lift Or Stairs?
text:
St Peter’s dome is a great climb. 550+ stairs gets you to the very top, where you have absolutely panoramic views over Rome. 
About halfway up, you come to the first level where there is a semi circular walkway around the inside of the dome. It has a high metal railings so it feels quite safe, although they do impede the view. From here we were able to have a birds-eye view down over the interior of the basilica and see the mosaic decoration up close, so close you could almost touch them.
We were intrigued by the lettering of the long inscription at the base of the dome. The letters are huge - 2 metres tall. It reads, “Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church. And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven”.
At this halfway point, you can also walk out to a large, open viewing platform.
If you are not up for climbing stairs, a lift will take you to this first level but if you want to continue right to the top, you’ll still have to climb about 300 stairs.
We climbed the whole way. With 550+ stairs, it was not easy and it’s  definitely not for the claustrophobic. 
The passage is narrow, steep and tight, with a low ceiling. It gets narrower as you go on and slowly spirals upwards until it is like a corkscrew set of stairs. At the very end it was almost dizzying. It’s one way only so there’s not really any option to back out once you’ve started.
If I was to do it again, I’d opt for the lift to the first level rather than climb the whole way. There was no real benefit to climbing to the first lot of stairs and it is only a very small amount extra for the lift.
Tickets are bought at the booth to the right of the basilica but you don’t need to pre-book. It’s €8 and €10 if you take the lift option.

title: Michelangelo, Bernini & Climbing the Dome
text:
Along with the Colosseum, St Peter’s Basilica tops the must-see list in Rome.
It is free to enter. No ticket or payment is needed but you have to wait in line to go through the security check. 
As expected, the line was long but it moved reasonably quickly and we could stand in the shade of the porticoes while we waited. 
The highlights inside are Michelangelo’s Pieta and Bernini’s monumental bronze baldachin. Mostly though, it was just the sheer scale of the place that completely overwhelmed us. If you ever want to be reminded that you that you are just a speck in the universe, this is the sort of place that will do it to you. Even looking back at photos, it is still amazing to see the ant-like size of the people in every photo.
Climbing the dome was incredible. The panoramic views from the top are not surprisingly jaw-dropping but I equally enjoyed the view from inside, looking down over the interior of the basilica. To climb the dome, you’ll need a ticket (€8). It is worth noting that there is a separate Tripadvisor listing for the dome.

text: Whether you visit on your own or end a tour here, it is a place to wander in view of its sheer size alone.  St Peter purportedly was buried inside the church built by Constantine the Great. Additions were made to the church during the Renaissance.  Masters like Bernini and Michelangelo are associated with its later changes. The Pieta, now behind bullet proof glass, is visible immediately on the right side. Next to it is the burial site of John Paul II. Many other popes are also buried here.  Fine works of art are available everywhere you look. Whether a believer or not, the site is of immense interest.

title: Basilica di San Pietro: история противостояния двух архитектурных концепций
text:
Вы никогда не задумывались – сколько в Риме храмов, церквей, базилик и прочих христианских культовых сооружений? Я вот тоже никогда об этом не задумывался, а оказалось, что в «Вечном городе» более  900 сакралов Христовых!!! Вдумайтесь в эти цифру – ДЕВЯТЬ СОТЕН... Именно поэтому столица Италии считается самым храмово-насыщенным городом в мире. 
На примере этого сакрального «созвездия» можно проследить бОльшую половину истории города «длинной» в 2774 года – начиная с 380 года, когда император Феодосий I Великий провозгласил христианство
государственной религией. И вот среди упомянутых девяти сотен сакралов есть один: самый центровой, самый огромный, самый величественный, самый почитаемый, самый известный... 
Вы наверняка уже догадались, что я говорю о Соборе Святого Петра что на римской Piazza San Pietro. Именно к нему я пришёл в первые часы своего пребывания в Риме – именно с этого объекта и начались мои «римские каникулы»... СтОя перед храмом, невольно вспомнил строки Анатолия Повшедного, посвящённые этому удивительному сооружению: «Здесь лучше просто думать и молчать, угадывая в сумраке столетия. Не от небес земная благодать: здесь смешаны легенды, мифы, сплетни...». 
Если честно, то мне очень не хотелось тратить время на рассказ о своём знакомстве с крупнейшим историческим христианским сакралом Земли – он запечатлён, описан, обследован и изучен как ни одно другое культовое сооружение Рима и Ватикана. А в повторении увиденного/услышанного/вычитанного просто не вижу смысла. Поэтому в рамках своего скромного поста остановлюсь лишь на паре интересных, nella mia profonda convinzione, моментов. 
История сакрала – это более пяти веков веры под его сводами, из которых полторы сотни лет ушло на возведение. И эти годы мега-стройки, на самом деле, были историей противостояния двух архитектурных концепций. С одной стороны – проект архитектора Донато Браманте, одного из создателей архитектуры римского классицизма XVI века с его центрическим типом крестово-купольных сооружений с «греческим крестом», заключённым в квадрат в основе плана. С другой – архитектурное видение Рафаэля Санти, одного из ярчайших представителей искусства эпохи Высокого Возрождения, отстаивавшего идею  традиционной формы плана сакрала в виде латинского креста.  
Греческий, как мы помним, это равносторонний крест, являющийся символом Христианской Церкви. Латинский же, символ Христовых страстей и искупление, есть крест, в котором продольная перекладина длиннее поперечной. Вы не поверите, но за всё время возведения Basilica di San Pietro «командиры» стройки менялись с завидной регулярностью, при этом каждый последующий придерживаться идеи, прямо противоположной предшествовавшей. То есть последователя Браманте однозначно сменял сторонник идей Санти. 
Перечень гуру от архитектуры, «приложивших руку» к возведению Собора Святого Петра, приводит в благоговейный трепет любого, кто хоть раз погружался в архитектурный «океан» римских must see. Один из крупнейших мастеров эпохи Возрождения и раннего барокко Микеланджело Буонарроти и военный инженер, скульптор флорентийской школы эпохи Возрождения Джулиано да Сангалло. Упоминавшиеся мной выше Донато Браманте и его извечный «антипандан» Рафаэль Санти. Гуманист, эрудит, архитектор, инженер, археолог, писатель, антиквар Фра Джованни Джокондо и флорентийский архитектор эпохи Высокого Возрождения Антонио да Сангалло Младший. 
Архитектор и живописец эпохи Высокого Возрождения и раннего маньеризма Бальдассаре Томмазо Перуцци и Бернардо Росселлино, скульптор и архитектор первой половины XV века. Архитектор и скульптор, один из наиболее значительных представителей маньеризма Джакомо делла Порта и архитектор-маньерист из Болоньи, один из самых влиятельных мастеров позднего Возрождения Джакомо Бароцци да Виньола. Художник, архитектор и антиквар XVI века Пирро Лигорио и  швейцарско-итальянский архитектор, яркий представитель римского барокко Карло Мадерна. И завершает этот удивительный сонм архитектурно-скульптурных гениев всех времён и народов Джованни Лоренцо Бернини – ни много, ни мало – создатель стиля барокко в скульптуре!!! 
На примере Собора Святого Петра запросто можно изучать полуторавековую историю итальянской архитектуры на примере творчества перечисленных мной гуру. И последний «штрих»: всем достоверно известно в направлении какой части света должна находиться апсидарная часть сакрала. Правильно – на востоке!!! Садитесь –  вам «пятёрка»!!! Только вот, в St. Peter's Basilica алтарная часть расположена на западе!!! Такой вот получается оксюморон...

1/5

Myself and sister were humiliated beyond belief. When paying the Dome cashier, (roughly 2pm) I was asked if I had a carer (as i hold a Blue Badge) I said yes, at this “Louis” the cashier told me to proceed through with her and her husband that had payed for his ticket. We were half way towards the Dome entrance when we were called back by another Security Guard who said it was the Ticket man called “Louis” discretion if Carer went in free. We were under the impression that this had all been sorted.  Does paying at the entrance with a Disabled Badge depend on if the face fits or, what nationality you are? Seems odd to me that admission falls on the shoulders of Cashier “Louis”. Correct Policy and Procedures were not consistent throughout the Vatican, as at the other entrance to the Vatican, a Carer Automatically goes in with the Blue Badge holder, no questions asked.
He then proceeded to shout very very loud and be Extremely Rude in front of Everyone, I told him it wasn’t an issue, happy to pay, but no! he carried on and on with the shouting in Italian (could of been talking Chinese, as I didn’t understand a Word!) My sister then told him how rude he was being, and should not be talking to the public (or anyone for that matter) like that especially working for the Vatican, a place of Piece and Tolerance! 
He needs Anger Management and lucky my husband wasn’t there, as “Louis” would been dealt with in a very different manner!!! Beware when buying tickets to the Dome people.
He needs to be Fired!! A Major Tourist Attraction should be aware of Protocols from other Countries (I’m sure I’m not the first British Blue Badge holder to have gone in)
Dome itself Amazing!

title: Incredible to behold - but book a Tour!
text: You can enter St.Peter's for Free, but you will spend a long time in a queue that can be avoided. If you book a tour then this will include a guide and the fast entry. We chose a tour that included the dome, cathedral and crypt. The Dome offers an astounding view of Rome. The first 200 steps are taken care of by an elevator, but the next few hundred you will have to climb yourself which is not easy. (Do not attempt this if you have health or mobility issues). If you just go to the first level you can still enjoy the view of the interior and the magnificent dome above - up close. title: Don't miss it!
text:
We had originally planned on visiting after our Vatican visit, but when we walked round to the Square the queue was 3/4 of the way round already. We therefore resolved to return early the next morning, and when we arrived at 8.30 there was hardly any queue so that was a good decision. 
Once through  the security gates (airport style) we went straight to the Basilica. You have to buy a ticket - 8 euro to walk the whole way or 10 euro to miss 200 steps and get the elevator. My advice is PAY THE EXTRA! The lift drops you out at basically roof level, behind the Bernini statues of the saints. There is a small souvenir shop and nice clean toilets, great views over the city and inside you can go about half-way round the dome, admiring the mosaics which replaced earlier paintings (due to atmospheric damage).  This is very securely fenced, but if you don't like heights then this is not the place for you.
Then up the remaining 300-odd steps to the top. In my view there are insufficient warnings before you start this climb: my husband and I are both in our 50s, and while not marathon runners are not unfit, but it was quite an undertaking. This is not just the number of steps, but it it very confined in places, very twisty (you're climbing inside a dome!) and even in the steepest bits nothing to hold onto - if anyone did suffer a health emergency I have no idea how they would get help to them , or remove them from this space. If you suffer from claustrophobia, breathing difficulties or are of a generous build be aware its one way up, one way down, very little opportunity to "pull over" for a breather. We were very glad to have visited in February rather than summer, but even then were quite hot and uncomfortable when we emerged onto the viewing gallery. The views are amazing of course!
We wound our way back down to explore the church - it is impossible to convey the sheer size and splendour. The artistry in all the carving and decoration is amazing,  yet it remains a very spiritual place.

So book a morning tour guide and get there early, we were there at 9am and it only took 10 minutes to get in. (At lunchtime there was may be a 500m que).
With the tour guide we were given an ear piece so we could listen to them talking privately and it worked really well.
Our Tour guide price to St Peters also included a trip to the roof top, we took the lift to the 1st part (good thing to do) then walked the rest. *Warning it's Steep and also as your climbing a dome you lean to one side. Also the last steps are tight spirall.
But when your there there are Fantastic views, my advice is take your time, don't panic and enjoy.
We also visited the crypt in the Basilica and visited past Pope's tombs.
Pope John Paul 2nd is here with many more very famous people.
A very special place to visit what ever your beliefs or politics,  Unbelievable architecture that needs to be seen.
YOU Will feel small trust me.
A must see.

title: Am 24.12.22 in der Heiligen Messe
text: Wir hatten das wahnsinnige Glück Zugang in die Heilige Messe am Heiligen Abend zu erhalten.  Ich möchte mich vorab bei Schwester Eva aus dem Vartikan bedanken. Sie hat uns dieses absolut einmalige Erlebnis ermöglicht 🙏 der Petersdom allein ist sicher eines der grössten Sehenswürdigkeiten der Welt. In Verbindung mit der Weihnachtsmesse war es für uns ein unvergessliches Erlebnis . Die Architektur aber natürlich auch die Messe mit der Anwesenheit des Pabstes wird uns den Rest unseres Lebens in Erinnerung bleiben. Einige Tips für den Besuch der Messe: Auf jeden Fall sehr Frühzeit vor Ort sein. Einlass war zwar erst ab 17 Uhr angekündigt , wir aber waren auf Rat von Schwester Eva schon um 13 Uhr dort.  Die Wartezeit hat sich gelohnt, denn nur so war es möglich recht weit vorn einen Platz zu bekommen. Es ist ziemlich unorganisiert und uns war nicht klar ob wir in der richtigen Schlange standen 😅  es waren leider sehr viele Besucher vor Ort die nicht wussten, dass man nur mit einer Einladung in die Messe gelangen konnte. Karten sind zu Weihnachten nicht käuflich zu erwerben. Diese bekommt man nur auf Anfrage direkt über den Vartikan ( auch nur wenn man Gluck hat)😄  Der Einlass auf den Petersdom ist dann auf der rechten Seite des Platzes!!!

title: When in Rome
text:

Audio guides are available to purchase - if not on a guided tour, definitely recommend this. To avoid steps (my parents are elderly) - walk toward the cloakroom and ask one of the staff to use the elevator to go up (have to say, not overly friendly staff manning the elevator, seemed to be a bit 'put out' when asked to use it! LOL, but to assist my parents mobility and avoid stairs I'll take a few teenage tuts!) After viewing what can only be described as the wonder of the Basilica in all its marble and gold, don't miss out on the tombs: Inside on the left of the basilica there is a small staircase to descend to see the tombs of previous popes. To see Pope John Paul II you follow this 'tunnel' and end up outside where you have to pay to get access to see his tomb. a bit sneaky I felt.

title: Con gli occhi protesi verso l'alto.
text:
Tra i luoghi più iconici di Roma, simbolo della cristianità nonché sincretismo d’arte, architettura e scultura senza eguali. Un luogo la cui storia si sviluppa lungo secoli custodendo segreti e meraviglie. 
Quando ci si trova di fronte ad una tale meraviglia come la Basilica di San Pietro in Vaticano, dopo essersi riempiti gli occhi di bellezza, il passo successivo è domandarsi cosa vedere. Sì, perché chiunque si avvicini a questo monumento, sintesi di duemila anni di storia del Cristianesimo, ma anche dell’arte e dell’architettura, non può non rimanere stordito di fronte cotanta ricchezza. 
La fila per entrare forse potrebbe essere un po' lunga ma ne vale la pena, ve lo assicuro.

title: Un chef d'oeuvre
text:
Depuis longtemps je rêvais d'aller voir la Chapelle Sixtine. Elle est incontournable à Rome, d'une beauté sans égale. 
Le seul mais tout de même gros problème : y accéder. 
Non pas parce qu'elle est bien cachée au sein du Vatican. Mais surtout parce que rien n'est fait pour la rendre "accessible" : il n'y a aucune gestion du flux des touristes. En cas de grosse affluance, tout le monde rentre en même temps, sort : on y "passe". Cela gâche sincèrement le plaisir d'y aller : on ne peut se poser et regarder, admirer. On est envahit par le monde plus que par la beauté du lieu. C'est fort dommage.
Il faut savoir que pour entrer au Vatican, il faut réserver. Toutefois, les réservations sont gérées "n'importe comment". Même si l'on réserve des billets coupe-file, on attend des heures. On pense avoir acheté des billets individuels alors qu'en fait, ce sont des billets de groupe et il faut attendre un groupe "virtuel" pour entrer. Bref, ce n'est pas l'idéal. Dans les périodes de grosses affluences, on se retrouve coincés dans une mare humaine : très stressant.
Mon avis pour profiter de la visite : éviter les périodes de vacances, y aller de bonne heure en réservant la 1ère tranche horaire, et se présenter longtemps à l'avance.

title: No apto para claustrofóbicos
text:
Llegamos a la plaza de San Pedro sobre las 15:00 horas, y entre el control de seguridad y lo que tuvimos que esperar para subir a la cúpula ya era de noche, ya que subimos sobre las 17 horas. A las 16 horas ya cerraron la puerta,  y no admitieron más visitas. Es decir, necesitamos unas 3 horas al final. A mí no se me hizo duro subir las escaleras, con ciertos descansos es bastante accesible a cualquiera con una forma física media. Lo mejor, ver la cúpula desde cerca y contemplar las dimensiones de la basílica desde arriba. Sin embargo, vimos que una de las chicas tuvo un ataque de ansiedad, suponemos que por claustrofobia. Hay partes de las escaleras que son bastante estrechas. A mí me dan miedo las alturas, pero está muy protegido, así que no tuve malas sensaciones. La vista desde arriba exterior es tan alta, que salvo la zona que da a la plaza de San Pedro, no me pareció tan espectacular como la esperaba. Dicen que desde arriba del Castelo de San Angelo las vistas de Roma son más bonitas. Lo dejaremos para nuestra próxima visita.
En resumen, si quieres subir a la cúpula ve a primera hora de la mañana y después aprovecha para ver la basílica. Si te agobian las estrecheces, puedes pasar un mal rato.

title: ÚNICA

Volvimos otro día para hacer una visita turística a nuestro aire, y acudimos a misa en la cátedra de Pedro. Hay varias misas al día en diferentes ubicaciones de la basílica, no se necesita reserva. Además también subimos a la cúpula, que te da una mayor conciencia de las dimensiones de este maravilloso templo. Me gustaría que la piedad de Miguel Ángel se pudiera contemplar más cerca y pudiendo rodearla, ya que solo se ve de frente y algo lejos. Hay mucha gente de seguridad y de orden, ya que la visitan muchas personas cada día. Estuvimos alrededor de una hora en la cola para pasar la seguridad. Si quieres evitar tanta cola, mejor ir a primerísima hora. Creo que abren a las 7 am.

title: Inspiring
text:
This was my second visit but my wife's first.

As a Catholic it was wonderful to be able to visit.

The queue on a weekday morning took about 45 minutes to clear.  It was a far more pleasant experience than standing in an Eiffel Tower, Paris queue for three hours.

The Basilica is superb, but remember, it's a House of God and so silence is best when inside.

It's so large that even though there may be 1,000 inspecting, it did not feel crowded.  Certainly different to the Church of England's Westminster Abbey in London.

La Pieta is for many a highlight, and sad, but I found some of the statues of most interest.

It was easy to catch the lift up to the observatory, but I didn't climb the stairs all the way to the dome.  

Great photos were taken outside, and again, this wasn't crowded.

We returned a second day only to go into the Basilica (free): this was an afternoon visit: only a very small queue.

A must-see in Rome, and paying the Euro10 for the lift was worth it.

Strangely the gift shop was closed.

title: grandeur & impressive!
text:
A must-see when in Rome and we were very surprised the crowd was NOT large on a Wednesday after lunch so the tour group grabbed the opportunity to go into the Basilica.  The security check was fast and we took only 15 mins of queuing, close to a miracle. [ normal q are an hour or more, being a major tourist attraction ]  
Simply overwhelming and mesmerized by the splendid and grandeur of the interior!  A sight to behold.  Once inside it t was high floor with impressive paintings, sculptures (masterpiece) and designed as a three-aisled Latin cross, directly above the high altar is the magnificent dome which covers the shrine of St. Peter the Apostle.
The largest church & most important place for Catholics in the world, St. Peter’s Basilica is a jewel within Vatican City. One of the most renowned works of Renaissance architecture and features many notable Baroque elements.  Besides being the focal point of millions of pilgrims-tourists the Basilica is also a cultural and historical and architectural landmark. We skipped the side trip of ascending up the steps to the top and also visiting the neighboring Sistine Chapel due to time constraint  There is simply too much to see and very where so nice to be captured by the camera.  Every corner every turn are marvelous treasures us. We simply stay still and gaze 360 dwg around us to absorb in the exhilarating atmosphere surround, that we are up-close and personal with history.
At the entrance there is a souvenir shop where we bought some postcards and stamps, but which we skipped.  From the entrance and looking out to St Peter’s Square we see the beautiful fountain and also the ancient Egyptian Obelisk.  It was centuries back that Bernini had designed the elliptical-shape piazza with the layout of many colonnades (row of 4), that serves as the approach to the main Basilica.  And on top of the tall decorated colonnade we had the opportunity to see the 12 Apostles & other statures that are above the front facade of the church.
Combining a scene of frocked priests, colorful Swiss Guards, large tourists crowd & flag-waving tour guides. Definitely another memento of our trip with the incredibly breath-taking sight. We left after just 2 hours for lunch and then the Colosseum.  A must-visit & bucket-list for many!

title: Beautiful! A highlight of a trip to the Vatican
text:
A wonderful experience! Don't be put off by the length of the queues - you can be seen to very quickly and it's always moving. The architecture and design is second to none; the staff were very friendly, and the ascent to the top is reasonably priced at 8 euros each for the stairs - 10 if you want to use the elevator for part of the way. We didn't pay for a tour, preferring to go round at our own pace, and I think we made the right call on that one.

***Wee note: if you're claustrophobic, think very carefully about the ascent up the steps to the top and whether you can hack it.*** I'm only mildly claustrophobic and three things that can set it off are elevators, crowds and tight corridors - so it was a bit "pick your poison" if I wanted to go up.  There are a couple of areas to perch if you need to take a breather, and I did have to at one point as I was stuck in a group of bodies all trying to climb up! The beautiful view at the top was worth it, we could stay as long as we liked and the way down was a lot easier on my nerves, but to others very nervous about tight spaces, just a heads up.

title: Amazing
text: We went to visit St Peters Basilica first thing on a Friday morning arriving at 8.30 am we knew it wouldn't be too busy at this time of the year but my wish was to go up the Dome we went early so it wouldn't be too crowded. Security to the right as you face St Peters Basilica and into the church entrance well signposted, left to church entrance and right to the Dome or Cupola as the Italians call it, keep right and then you can see a tiny kiosk. You can pay cash or card now to go up the Dome. We used the elevator that was 10€ each. Once past the elevator you can reach the inside of Michelangelo’s Dome which was spectacular, all tiny mosaics which look just as though he'd painted them. I didn’t find the climb up to the top of the Dome too arduous although there are little places you can stand to catch your breath if needed. The views are stunning and not to be missed 360° walk around and some places to sit and take it all in. Back down a different set of steps you come back to the elevators but before you leave there are toilets which I can say the ladies were very clean, a cafe which we didn't go in and a souvenir shop where we bought some postcards and stamps. We wrote on them and posted in the little yellow post box outside the shop. Another memento of our trip. We had the opportunity to see the Twelve Apostles that are above the front facade of the church, you certainly realise how large they are up close. Down the elevator and straight into St Peters Basilica no queuing at all. Wow, it is beautiful just heavenly divine from the ceiling to the marble floor. The Pietà statue by Michelangelo had a small crowd not too bad but it was now 10am and starting to get busy with lots of tours walking around. Inspiring, beautiful place to contemplate and reflect.

title: Nádhera za cenu davu lidí
text:
Prohlídka Vatikánu rozhodně stojí za to. Bohužel se člověk musí zařadit do dlouhé fronty, kde vás každou chvíli obtěžují prodejci skupinových, velice predrazenych prohlídek. 
Pokud se zařadite do fronty cca v 15:30, začne se velmi rychle hýbat, jelikož se blíží konec otevírací doby a personál se snaží pustit co nejvíce lidí - takže místo x hodinového stání ve frontě tam strávíte cca 30 minut.
Po koupení lístků v horním patře budovy si můžete projít krátký/dlouhý (7km) okruh. My zvolili dlouhý a ač to bylo náročné a snad nekonečné, viděli jsme toho opravdu spoustu.
Na závěr Sistinska kaple, kde se v jako jediné místnosti nesmí fotit. Uhrane svojí velikostí, nádherou a má co nabídnout.
Bohužel po celou dobu je nutné se prodírat davy lidí, hlavně organizovaných skupin, a všichni směřují právě do kaple, kde je to v tomto množství lidí naprosté šílenství. 
Tento unikát má tedy svoji daň v podobě silně přeplněné kapacity. Proto 4/5.
Mimochodem, stejně krásné a snad ještě větší malované stropy a celé budovy lze vidět téměř v každém kostele a to zadarmo, bez lidí.

title: Buy a post card and save money
text: The whole visit does not appear to have changed since I was there 15 years ago. Crowds being force fed into narrow corridors after being shepherded past acres of cluttered halls with souvenir shops on every corner. School groups, tourist parties and people like us who fell for the hype sweated their way into the tiny chapel and stared at the ceiling, all looking for the iconic picture of the finger of God. The picture is not as big as you think it would be, either - again, misleading images have been promoted! It is the size of all the others and takes a moment to pick out. I heard muttering from the other visitors, "Is that it!"  Also photographs are being taken despite the almost hysterical orders coming from the loud speakers. That's right, loudspeakers in an area where there is supposed to hushed reverence! We were glad to get out of there! Save your money!

title: Wunderschön, aber nichts für Besucher mit Platzangst
text:
Vorab: Ich bewerte hier nicht die Kapelle an sich - denn die ist nicht bewertbar -, sondern nur meinen Besuch dort.
Ich habe mich so sehr darauf gefreut und konnte es kaum erwarten.

Leider wurde das Erlebnis fast zu einem Alptraum, denn der Massentourismus findet hier seinen Höhepunkt. Man wird auf dem Weg in die Kapelle immer wieder auf Schildern darauf hingewiesen, dass dies ein heiliger Ort ist und man sich dementsprechend verhalten soll. Also Ruhe (unser Guide sagte, dass er uns in der Kapelle nichts erklären wird, da Sprechen dort verboten ist) und kein Fotografieren. 
Sobald man aber die Kapelle betritt, wird man sofort von Polizisten angebrüllt, dass man weitergehen und nicht stehenbleiben soll. Es ist auch gar nicht anders möglich, denn durch die drängelnden Menschenmassen wird man automatisch weitergeschoben. Die Kapelle ist nicht sehr groß und platzte regelrecht aus allen Nähten. Eine ruhige und ausgiebige Betrachtung des Werks Michelangelos ist so nicht möglich. 
Es wird gebrüllt, geredet, gelacht und natürlich auch fotografiert, das Personal schreit die ganze Zeit die Leute an etc. 
Ich habe dann beim rausgehen auch regelrechte Platzangst und fast eine Panikattacke bekommen, weil sich alle Besucher durch eine kleine Tür quetschen müssen. Wirklich grauenhaft.
Mit einem heiligen Ort hat das alles überhaupt gar nichts mehr zu tun. Ich weiß aber auch keine Lösung dieses Problems, da jeden Tag mehrere 10.000 Menschen die Kapelle besichtigen wollen. Aber für den Besucher ist das alles traurig und eine einzige Enttäuschung. Das hat dieser wunderschöne Ort einfach nicht verdient.

... voilà la première impression quand on pénètre dans la chapelle Sixtine. Les photos ont beau être interdites et le silence requis (nous sommes dans une chapelle ne l'oublions pas), les touristes munis d'un smartphone jouent au jeu du chat et de la souris avec les gardes et le brouhaha oblige ces mêmes gardes à répéter en boucle "silence et "silenzio" sans grand effet.
Reste malgré tout les fresques de Michel-Ange pour lesquelles l'audio-guide n'est pas superflu afin d'apprécier tous les détails auxquels on ne prêterait pas attention sans et qui valent le coup d’œil !
A noter que la chapelle Sixtine clôt la visite des musées du Vatican donc vous ne pouvez pas faire l'un sans l'autre (sauf le cas échéant dans le cadre d'une visite guidée qui exclurait les musées).
Si vous vous faufilez ni vu ni connu avec un groupe, vous pourrez accéder directement à la basilique Saint-Pierre sans avoir à refaire la queue mais vous louperez le magnifique escalier à double révolution qui conduit vers la sortie classique. C'est à vous de voir !

title: Sublime souvenir. A voir absolument.
text:
La Chapelle Sixtine est mondialement connue. Elle tient son nom du Pape Sixtine IV qui l’a fait construire.C’est dans cette salle que sont élus les Papes. Les plafonds qui ont été peints par Michel Ange en personne qui, durant quatre ans, c’est échiné à créer ce chef d’œuvre. Echiné est le bon terme car le dos et les vertèbres du Maître ne se remettront jamais de la position de travail imposée. En cherchant bien, vous verrez que le peintre c’est représenté dans sa peinture ( au centre, sous Dieu, un vieillard barbu qui tient une peau d’homme pendouillante, c’est lui).
Pendant ce temps, Raphaël, pour sa part, peignait à quelques dizaines de mètres de là les nouveaux appartements privés du Pape qui refusait d’habiter là ou le Pape Borgia avait vécu.
Il est impossible de filmer ou de prendre des photos à l’intérieur car les droit d’images sont la propriété d’une société japonaise qui a payé à grands frais la restauration à 99,99999% des peintures. Les 0,00001% restant sont des petits rectangles noircis qui témoignent de l’état avant restauration.
A voir absolument . C’est splendide.

title: Set your alarm and avoid the queue
text: It’s Rome’s #1 attraction for a reason - it is utterly spectacular inside and out. We chose to get up super early and get to St Peter’s Square for 7am when the doors open (you can join the queue beforehand if you’re there even earlier). This meant we got sunrise over the square and only queued for 5 minutes to get through the scanners before going in to a nearly empty basilica. We were there an hour and by the time we left the queue was probably at least 45 minutes - it’s worth the wait if you queue, but if you don’t have the time or patience, getting there early is the best option, or you can book a tour of the Vatican Museums that includes entrance via the side door to St Peter’s - this was shut during covid, but was definitely being used in October 2022.

title: What difference will my review make?  If you want to see it, there are no options.
text:
I've been to it twice.  I've never been inside of it.  Both times I went they had something scheduled that was not published on their website.  

It's Italy.  If you expect them to maintain their web presence, well, you've clearly never been to Italy.  In their minds, the Pope's audience (or whatever) has been known for weeks.  The fact that they didn't publish it?

Come back some other time.  

And, btw, you only learn that you can't get in *after* you get through their Italian-Style security procedure.  I hope you have many hours to burn, just to find out "is not possible to enter, today."  

I've been to the Sistine Chapel twice and it is mind blowing.  I've been across the angel bridge many times, it's great.  The outside of the Basilica is very pretty.  But both times I've tried to get in I've been met by bureacracy.  By pre-scheduled "we're not open to the public, today" activities that were not published online - and I checked as I stood there, outside.

title: Visita obligada
text: La entrada a la Basílica de San Pedro en el Vaticano es una visita imprescindible cuando se viaja a Roma. La cola para entrar, aunque pueda parecer interminable, va bastante rápido y cuando te quieres dar cuenta ya estás accediendo al interior. Además, esta recorre la plaza de San Pedro por lo que, mientras esperas, te puedes entretener observando el lugar. El interior es tan impactante que, a pesar de que se puede estar todo el tiempo que quieras, es imposible apreciarlo todo de una vez. Concretamente, dentro puedes disfrutar de obras desde Bernini a Miguel Ángel, el interior de la cúpula, ver la tumba de San Pedro y acceder a las grutas vaticanas. A raíz del COVID-19, sin embargo, algunas experiencias han quedado limitadas, como tocar el pie de la escultura de San Pedro, que ya no es posible. Además, nos llamó la atención que, en nuestra visita, La Piedad de Miguel Ángel estuvo tapada con unas cortinas hasta las 11:30, aunque desconocemos si es algo habitual. En cualquier caso, la visita a la basílica es una experiencia espectacular para repetir!

title: Do the early entrance ticket! Remarkable.
text: We've visited the Sistine Chapel a half dozen times. This time, we bought the early entrance ticket (you enter about 7:30 a.m, about 90 minutes before the crowds). The Chapel is a remarkable experience at any time. But it is so much more sacred, and stunning, when you are one of about 30 people in the chapel. Rather than the thousands when general admission begins. It is well worth the extra tariff for the tour guide/company. Such a different experience.... to be able to look at the Last Judgement, without jostling and the crowd noise, for nearly as long as you wish. The early entrance allows you to truly appreciate the art of a sacred place. Without the booming "Silenzio" from the guards trying to silence the pushing crowds. It's a bucket list visit. Worth the extra cost.

title: Capilla Sixtina y Museos del Vaticano
text:
Fuimos cuatro personas y tuvimos muy mala experiencia, después de esperar horas en una cola para comprar los tickets para visitar los museos y la capilla Sixtina.

Fue muy desagradable, entramos en los Museos Vaticanos como rebaños todos apelotonados sin poder casi ni andar unos contra otros era imposible parar y disfrutar las maravillas que había porque te estaban empujando continuamente para seguir andando.

La siguiente visita es cuando llegas en masa a la capilla Sixtina la palabra agobio es insignificante, estaba totalmente lleno no te podías apenas ni mover, y unos señores indicándote cual es la puerta de salida para ir  al exterior y si lo deseas puedes vuelves a hacer otra cola para entrar a la Basílica,
Pero sin embargo si entras en un grupo con guía incluido y pagas algo más por la entrada, entonces la salida de la Capilla es por otra puerta diferente y te llevan sin hacer cola a la Basílica

En definitiva ha sido la peor visita turística que he tenido estos días en Roma, me dio la sensación  que los turistas que entramos    no pudimos disfrutar y aprender de la belleza de su patrimonio, me parecio solo un afán de recaudar y recaudar sin límite de control de entrada, pues incluso cuando nosotros salimos aún seguía habiendo cola y entrando más gente. 
Realmente no me enteré de nada, salimos peor que entramos y pensamos ..... que pena del dinero gastado, podíamos haberlo disfrutado de otra forma.
En fin una mala experiencia, a compartir

La fila, fatta di giovedì alle 11.30 è durata circa mezz'ora. Alla cassa abbiamo preso la salita in ascensore(costo 10 euro Vs 8 facendo an he i primi 200 scalini a piedi) al termine ci siamo fatti gli ultimi 320 scalini a piedi, il bimbo di 5 anni senza problemi, io ero affaticata alla fine, ma avevo al bimba legata a me. La salita 6 non è consigliata a chi ha problemi circolatorio o cardiaci. Si può vedere dall'alto l'interno della basilica di San Pietro e, arrivato in cima, Roma in tutto il suo splendore. title: Not how great art should be viewed
text:
I am fortunate (and old enough!) to have visited the chapel in 1971. I recall two things: I was awed by the frescoes; and the silence. 
Revisiting the chapel 48 years later was a wholly different experience. While the art of Michelangelo not only has not diminished in its greatness, the cleaning has made it brighter and truer to the original.
Nevertheless, I must say that my recent visit left me with the feeling that I get when I enter a professional sports facility for a big game. It was incredibly loud and claustrophobically crowded. Despite the word “SILENCIO!” being sternly voiced over the loudspeakers, the crowd continued talking, even shouting, showing absolutely no respect for  the artwork or the place. After all it is a chapel. 
It’s all really unfortunate. It’s not the way it should be experienced. The Vatican could learn from the Villa Borghese, which allows only a limited number of visitors in every two hours. I realize this would restrict the number of people, and as well, the income, but it would be a much better experience.

Il fut un temps où on pouvait ne visiter que La Chapelle Sixtine dans les musées du Vatican.
Maintenant, c’est fini.
Vous êtes tenu de visiter l’ensmble des musées du Vatican pour accéder à La Chapelle. Il s’en suit un long parcours impossible à réaliser pour une personne âgée par exemple, pollué par les groupes, l’affluence, les bruits insupportables dans un musée de guides qui parlent fort, de jeunes qui traversent les salles en plaisantant, de gardiens qui bavardent entre eux. On ne voit cela dans aucun musée chez nous. On est aussi frustré de devoir visiter au pas de charge des musées fort intéressants mais il ne faut pas perdre de temps si on veut voir La Chapelle Sixtine en ayant encore envie après plusieurs heures de visite et des kilomètres fatigants parcourus.
Enfin, quand on arrive dans l’immense Chapelle Sixtine, quelles surprises ! Je ne décrirai pas l’oeuvre, c’est fait dans tous les commentaires, mais seulement l’ambiance.
On se trouve au sein d’une foule de visiteurs massés les uns sur les autres sans pouvoir se déplacer. Le bruit ambiant est énorme, les gens parlent tous entre eux. Quelques gardiens en uniforme surveillent que nul ne prend de photos. Toutes les deux ou trois minutes, un haut parleur hurle littéralement qu’il ne faut prendre ni photos, ni vidéos.
Sue l’appréciation des peintures, il est très difficile de suivre les explications données par l’audioguide, tant elles sont confuses ( passage d’un côté à l’autre, description de scènes ou de tableaux difficilement visibles car on est éloignés et qu’on ne peut pas physiquement se rapprocher vue la foule ambiante).
Bref, quand on sort de La Chapelle on est ala fois déçus et émerveillé.
Je retiens les motifs de déception car ceux ci seraient largement perfectibles en organisant mieux cette visite.

Je conseille enfin de venir avec un plan papier sur lequel les différents tableaux et scènes seront décrits, afin de mieux comprendre la signification des scènes des Testaments représentés. Renoncez aux audioguides, ce n’est qu’une source de tracas. Claustrophobes s’abstenir.

title: Beautiful...Wish it was earlier in the tour
text: We took a tour of The Vatican, Sistine Chapel and St. Peter’s Basilica with a small group of about 15. The tour guide was very informative and definitely had a passion for every detail. The problem was, we had been touring for about 90 minutes before we got to the Sistine Chapel and every ceiling to that point was beautiful with either architectural detail or frescos. So once you get to the Sistine Chapel, although amazing, it felt like very much of the same. It is TOTALLY worth seeing, but just be aware you may have overload before making it to the actual Chapel. Right after the Sistine Chapel is St. Peter’s Basilica. The most beautiful place I have ever seen in my life. I understand the logic of the tour order...but, selfishly, wish it was in reverse. Also, you are allowed to take pictures until you get to the Chapel and it wasn’t very clear photos were NOT allowed in there. Be ready for security to quickly tell you to put away your camera. I learned the hard way!
