title: Vatican from the roof
text: We pre booked our tour of St. Peters Basilica within a package which included the Dome, roof, Sistine Chapel and Vatican museum. This tour was a bit more expensive but well worth it. Skip the line at the Vatican isn’t straight to the front there is still a short wait? The first part of the tour lasted 2 hours and exploded the basilica, it’s roof, the top of dome and catacombs. The interior of the basilica was breathtaking. After a lift up to the roof you get an amazing view of St. Peter’s square and surrounding streets. Next was the climb to the top of the dome. This is for those amongst us that can handle heights and the 300+ steps ( need a reasonable level of fitness to get to the top). Once at the top it’s a once in a lifetime view. The second half of the tour was at the Vatican museum and Sistine chapel. Amazing museum but the crowds limit your views of some exhibits. The Sistine chapel is beautiful but again the crowds were overwhelming! Our guide Sandra was so knowledgeable, informative and helpful 10/10. If you get the chance this tour is a must.

title: Extremely rude and unprofessional staff member
text: Shocking staff behaviour. Me and my husband wanted to buy the audio guides at the Basilica. We asked a member of staff, called Valentia, how much they cost. She explained that the audio guides were 15€ with the Dome included. We asked if we could have a think and come back, she said yes. We then went back to buy them as we thought 15€ each for audio guides and entrance to the Dome was a good price. We went to the Dome entrance and waited in line for about 10 minutes, we then showed the guard the receipt for the audio guide, thinking it was our ticket, and he explained that that was just for the audio guide and the entrance for the Dome was an extra 8€. We went back to Valentia to have a refund, as we thought 15€ just for the audio guide was extortionate. When we got to her desk, my husband said, very politely and calmly, that we didn’t understand that the price didn’t include the Dome, so we would like a refund. Valentia immediately began shouting at us, in an incredibly aggressive tone: “I will not give you a refund!” My husband explained that it had only been 10 minutes and that we hadn’t used the guides yet. Valentia put her hand up rudely and told us to wait. She then began serving another customer and speaking to that customer, very rudely, about us. She also turned to her colleague and talked about us extremely rudely again. Her colleague laughed at us. Being Portuguese, I can understand almost everything in Italian, so found this extremely offensive. When Valentia finished talking about us and serving the customer, she began shouting at us again and said “I EXPLAINED TO YOU TWICE THAT THIS DOESN’T MEAN YOU HAVE THE TICKET, YOU HAVE TO THINK TWICE BEFORE YOU DO ANYTHING IN LIFE! I SPOKE ENGLISH TO YOU DIDN’T I?!” Valentia proceeded to make a huge scene, shouting at us, as we stared at her in disbelief. My husband asked if we could have a refund and she gave us our money back and started saying “Ciao” repeatedly at us. I asked her if I could have my ID card back, as she had taken it when we bought the audio guides, and she threw it in my hands extremely aggressively. She then resumed her shouting, repeating that we needed to think twice and that she was only doing her job. My husband tried to explain that we were not complaining, that we knew it was our misunderstanding, but Valentia did not let him speak and began waving at us and saying “Ciao”. We left and visited the Basilica, which was wonderful, although hugely spoilt by this hurtful experience. This employee’s immediately defensive behaviour, when we were simply politely asking for a refund led us to, on reflection, believe that this audio guide situation might be a scam. These are the official selling points after you enter security and there are no prices on show. The staff (or just Valentia) don’t make it too clear that you’re buying a ticket that doesn’t include the Dome. After waiting in line to see the Dome, it is highly likely that the majority of people will just pay the extra, on top of the extortionate 15€ for audio guides and not bother to go back. Be careful.

title: Basilica & Dome
text: The size of St. Peter's Basilica is the first thing you will notice when you walk inside this architectural wonder. It reminds how small we really are. Entry to Saint Peter's basilica is free. If you want to climb the dome, the entrance to St. Peter's dome is to the right of the entrance to St. Peter's Basilica. It costs 8 Euros to climb via the stairs (about 200 steps), and 10 Euros to take the lift (to the 1st level), and wind up on the inside of Michelangelo's dome. Here you can look down on the inside of St. Peter's Basilica from above. As for the second part climbing to the dome, there are another 300 steps to the top. This part could be a bit claustrophobic for some and there is no lift option. It's a narrow single-file staircase climb that slowly spirals up, with the roof sort of slanting in towards you as you go. But the view is well worth the effort. Sad to see some people continue to leave their marks on the wall though. If you do not plan to visit the Vatican Museums, and will only visit St. Peter's Basilica, you should visit the dome before the basilica because you come into the basilica when you exit the dome. Enjoy your visit!

title: Ein Must-See
text:
Wir haben den Petersdom besucht, sowie die Aussichtsplattform der Kuppel. Beides sehr sehenswert. Bevor man jedoch zum Petersdom kommt muss man durch die Sicherheitskontrolle, dies kann je nach Uhrzeit, etwas länger dauern. Wir haben uns extra entsprechend den Vorschriften knielang und schulterbedeckt gekleidet. Wir hatten jedoch das Gefühl, dass sie bei der Knielänge nicht mehr so streng kontrollieren, sowie den Gästen eine Bedeckung zur Verfügung stellen. 

Von der Kuppel hat man eine einzigartige Aussicht. Um zur Aussichtsplattform zu gelangen hat man die Auswahl zwischen 2 Tickets. Eines ohne Aufzug, welches 8€ kostet und eines mit Aufzug, welches 10€ kostet. Wir haben das Ticket mit Auszug gewählt, weil man auch danach noch um die 300 Stufen zu Fuß gehen muss. Das Treppenhaus ist teilweise wirklich sehr eng und immer Sommer sehr stickig. Wir waren zum Glück gleich morgens gegen 08:30 Uhr dort, da war es noch auszuhalten. Die Aussicht ist den Aufstieg jedoch absolut wert.

Anschließend haben wir den Petersdom besichtigt. Natürlich sollte man sich dies auch nicht entgehen lassen, wenn man schon dort ist.
